Cloudland Canyon State Park: Hikes, Waterfalls & Caves

Original Author: Jack Byrum
Read time: 8 minutes
Last updated: 11/21/2026
Published on: 12/24/2024
Geo coverage: Rising Fawn, GA and surrounding area (Walker County GA, Dade County GA, within 35 miles of Chattanooga, TN)
Seasonality: Year-round; best weather March-November, waterfalls peak after rainfall
#outdoors#interactive

Get our local guides and events updates.

This guide covers 19 trails, activities, and dining spots at Cloudland Canyon State Park and nearby. The park sits in Rising Fawn, Georgia, about 35 miles south of Chattanooga. It covers over 3,500 acres on the western edge of Lookout Mountain.
Six hiking trails are listed here, from a one-mile overlook walk to a six-mile descent into the gorge. The Waterfalls Trail drops over 600 metal grate stairs to Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls. The West Rim Loop has ranked as one of the top hikes in the United States in multiple years.
Mountain biking centers on the 5 Points Recreation Area, a few miles east of the main park entrance. Four route options are listed here, from an easy 3-mile loop to an expert 5-mile ride. The park rents bikes at the Visitor Center for $35 half day or $55 full day.
The Activity filter separates hiking, mountain biking, and dining. The Difficulty filter narrows to easier or challenging options. The Kids filter surfaces six spots well-suited for families. The park charges a $5 daily parking fee and is open 7am to 10pm year-round.
If there is a trail or activity worth adding, send an email. Details change. Confirm before you go.

Hiking at Cloudland Canyon.

Six hiking trails are listed here, from one mile to six miles. Three are easier and accessible to most visitors. The West Rim Loop is the signature trail, nearly five miles along the canyon rim with views throughout. The Waterfalls Trail is the hardest and most rewarding — 600-plus metal stairs lead to Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls at the bottom of the gorge. Sitton’s Gulch is the most remote, following creek valleys through spring wildflowers with far fewer people on the trail.

Chattanooga outdoors guide

Mountain Biking at 5 Points.

The 5 Points Recreation Area sits a few miles east of the main park entrance. The network has 20-plus miles of trail ranging from green to expert. The Cloudland Canyon Connector (CCC) is the main spine of the system, linking all the other trails. Two easier routes and two advanced routes are listed here. The park rents bikes at the Visitor Center for $35 half day or $55 full day. Call ahead to confirm availability.

Chattanooga outdoors guide

Cloudland Canyon with Kids.

Six activities here are well-suited for families with children. The Meadowlands and Overlook trails are both one mile and easy to complete. The fishing pond is stocked with catfish and requires no license. The 18-hole disc golf course is included with park entry. The park also keeps an all-terrain Action Trackchair and EnChroma glasses for visitors with mobility or color-vision needs — ask at the park office to reserve either one.

Eating Near the Park.

Three restaurants are within 10 to 15 minutes of the park. Hope House Cafe handles breakfast and lunch. Canyon Grill is the dinner option but is closed Sunday and Monday, so plan your visit day around that. Thatcher’s BBQ is the most casual and handles lunch or dinner. Several North Georgia breweries and wineries are also within 30 minutes of the park.

Clear filters

1. Meadowlands Trail .

One-mile out-and-back trail near the disc golf parking area. An observation deck offers canyon views along the route. Blackberry bushes line the path in summer. The park fishing pond sits off this trail. No fishing license is required at the pond.
Google Maps
#hiking #easy #main-park #kids

2. Overlook Trail .

One-mile out-and-back trail that starts at the main parking lot. Easy to find and quick to complete. Views of the canyon are good in spring and fall. A good first trail for new visitors or anyone getting back into hiking.
Google Maps
#hiking #easy #main-park #kids

3. Backcountry Loop Trail .

Two-mile loop that connects to the park's primitive campsites. Rated 4.6 out of 5 on AllTrails. Less trafficked than the main trails. No direct trailhead pin exists. Park at the disc golf lot and use the trail map. Bring waterproof footwear.
Google Maps AllTrails
#hiking #easy #main-park

4. West Rim Loop .

4.7-mile loop that follows the canyon rim. This trail has ranked among the top hikes in the country in multiple years. Canyon views appear throughout the route. Rugged terrain. Proper footwear is required. Best at golden hour for sunset views.
Google Maps
#hiking #challenging #main-park

5. Waterfalls Trail .

1.8-mile trail accessed from the West Rim Loop. The most strenuous trail in the park. Over 600 metal grate stairs lead down to Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls. Not recommended for dogs due to the stairs. Water flow is best after heavy rain.
Google Maps
#hiking #challenging #main-park #waterfalls

6. Sitton's Gulch Trail .

Six-mile out-and-back trail that descends into the valley and follows creek paths. Spring wildflowers add to the experience. Fewer crowds than other trails in the park. Sitton's Cave is nearby. Guided cave tours run in select months. Book ahead to combine both in one day.
Google Maps
#hiking #challenging #main-park

7. Bankhead + CCC + Shale Flats Loop (MTB) .

Three-to-four-mile loop using three easy-rated trails in the 5 Points network. Total climb is roughly 125 to 250 feet. Plan for about 20 to 30 minutes of riding. All three trails run in both directions. Park at 5 Points and start on Bankhead.
Google Maps
#mountain-biking #easy #5-points

8. Cloudland Canyon Connector Out and Back (MTB) .

6.8-mile out-and-back on the most popular trail in the 5 Points system. Green-rated the entire way. Park at Ascalon Trailhead and follow the CCC at every fork. The trail ends at Hinkie Road. Turn around and return the same way. Bike rentals are available at the Visitor Center for $35 half day or $55 full day.
Google Maps
#mountain-biking #easy #5-points

9. Tailings Run + CCC + North Hogsback (MTB) .

Four-to-five-mile loop combining two expert-rated trails with the easy CCC connector. Start at 5 Points on Tailings Run (1.5 miles, expert), then link to CCC. Turn onto North Hogsback (1.1 miles, expert) to return to the 5 Points lot. Expect technical features and significant climbing.
Google Maps
#mountain-biking #challenging #5-points

10. Bankhead + Kettle Bottom (MTB) .

Five-to-six-mile route from 5 Points. Start on Bankhead (0.4 miles) to CCC, then onto Kettle Bottom (intermediate). Kettle Bottom can be ridden as a full loop or a shorter alternate. Return via CCC and Bankhead. A good step up from the easy network routes.
Google Maps
#mountain-biking #challenging #5-points

11. Disc Golf Course .

18-hole course about 5 minutes from the park entrance. Concrete tees and a marked layout. Some sections are reported as overgrown. No additional fee beyond the $5 park entry. No restrooms directly on the course. Park at the dedicated disc golf lot.
Google Maps
#main-park #kids

12. Camping .

The park offers yurts, cabins, RV sites, and primitive backcountry campsites. Yurts and cabins book out first. Reserve a few weeks ahead for spring and fall weekends. Check the Georgia State Parks site for current availability and pricing.
Google Maps Reserve a Site
#main-park #kids

13. Fishing Pond .

One-acre pond stocked with channel catfish. No fishing license is required. Catch-and-keep season runs from the day after Labor Day through the end of November. All other times are catch and release. Fishing in the park's creeks is not allowed. Easiest access is via the Meadowlands Trail.
Google Maps
#main-park #kids

14. Hope House Cafe .

Breakfast and lunch cafe about 10 to 15 minutes from the park. Run by A Hand Up Ministry. Good atmosphere for a post-hike meal. Check hours before visiting.
Google Maps
#dining #near-park

15. Canyon Grill .

Dinner-only restaurant 5 to 10 minutes from the park. Closed Sunday and Monday. Known for seafood, steaks, and fried okra. The most upscale option near the park. Plan your visit day around their hours.
Google Maps
#dining #near-park

16. Thatcher's BBQ And Grille .

BBQ restaurant serving lunch and dinner. Menu includes brisket and banana pudding. Gluten-free options are available. A casual post-hike stop near the park.
Google Maps
#dining #near-park

17. Cave Tours (Sitton's Cave) .

A park naturalist leads guided trips into Sitton's Cave. No lights or handrails inside. Expect to crawl through mud and scramble over rocks. Tours run in April, June, July, September, and October. Cost is $45 per person, ages 10 and up. Each tour lasts about 2 to 2.5 hours. Call 706-657-4050 to book. Experienced cavers can apply for a permit to explore Case Cave, which requires ropes and harnesses.
Google Maps
#main-park #seasonal

18. Horseback Riding .

Certain trails in the 5 Points Recreation Area allow horseback riding. No guided horse tours are offered by the park. You must bring your own horse. Park and load at Ascalon Trailhead. Check the trail map for horse-approved routes before your visit.
Google Maps
#5-points

19. Picnic Areas .

Free picnic tables are scattered throughout the park. Covered shelters can be reserved for events or family gatherings. Reserve shelters on the Georgia State Parks site. Shelters require a separate reservation fee.
Google Maps Reserve a Shelter
#main-park #kids
The 5 Points Recreation Area has its own parking and trailhead, a few miles east of the main park entrance. Plan to move your car between the two areas if you want to hike and bike on the same trip.
Camping books fast in spring and fall. Yurts and cabins sell out first. Reserve a few weeks ahead for peak season weekends. Check the Georgia State Parks site for availability.

FAQ.

Do you need a fishing license at Cloudland Canyon?

No license required. The park pond is stocked with channel catfish. Catch and keep runs from the day after Labor Day through the end of November. All other times are catch and release. Fishing in the park’s creeks is not allowed.

Can you rent bikes at Cloudland Canyon?

Yes. The Visitor Center rents mountain bikes for $35 half day or $55 full day. Call ahead to confirm availability before making the drive.

Can you bring dogs to Cloudland Canyon?

Dogs are welcome on most trails on a leash no longer than 6 feet. The Waterfalls Trail is not recommended for dogs. The 600-plus metal grate stairs can be painful and difficult for them to navigate.

When do the cave tours run?

Guided wild cave tours of Sitton’s Cave run in April, June, July, September, and October. Each tour lasts about 2 to 2.5 hours and costs $45 per person, ages 10 and up. Call 706-657-4050 to book. Experienced cavers can get a permit for Case Cave, which requires ropes and harnesses.

What waterfalls are in Cloudland Canyon?

The park has two main waterfalls: Hemlock Falls and Cherokee Falls. Both are reached via the Waterfalls Trail, which branches off the West Rim Loop. Flow varies with rainfall and is strongest after a heavy storm.

Can you swim at Cloudland Canyon?

There is no designated swimming area in the park. The waterfalls and creek pools are not set up for swimming. The fishing pond is stocked for fishing only.
